methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $13M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Sarla Aviation is a Series A-stage transportation company that has raised $13M to date. The broader transportation sector comp universe includes eight private peers—notably Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Pipedream, and FleetZero—with no public comparables available. This limited public market reference point constrains valuation methodology options.

Given the absence of sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage peers within transportation meeting minimum density thresholds (fewer than three datapoints per filter), a peer-median approach is not reliably applicable. Instead, the valuation relies on stage-progression methodology, which applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier to the $13M total raised as a proxy for post-Series A value. This method yields an implied valuation of $26M. The triangulated range, derived from single-method sensitivity analysis, spans $22M (low) to $30M (high), with a median of $26M.

Key uncertainties center on the limited comparable dataset and the absence of public market anchors for the transportation sector. The stage-progression multiplier reflects typical venture-stage advance patterns but may not capture Sarla Aviation's specific unit economics, technology maturity, or market positioning relative to the broader peer set. Sensitivity to the 2.0x multiplier assumption and validation against transaction comps or revenue multiples—if available—would strengthen conviction in this range.
